Priya Shah: Quick heads-up  ember-x-int4 canary this morning: structured-output parse failures that look like a rogue terminator character appended after a well-formed funcall JSON. Only happens when stream=true and small batches.
Liam Foster: Can you paste an example capture?
Priya Shah: Raw stream fragment below. Note the JSON is fine but there's a trailing literal NUL-ish byte and sometimes the sequence `\x00\n`. Parsers that validate exact bytes fail.
Priya Shah: ```
{"tool":"annotate","args":{"text":"..."}}
\u0000
```
Natalie Ortiz: That's nasty. Do we have token traces showing the model emitted that control code or is runtime inserting it?
Priya Shah: Token trace suggests model tokens include an explicit 0x00 token at the end of some completions: `[TOK_2102]="}" [TOK_2103]="\\x00"`. Canary mirror to raven-v2 (non-quant) had 0% failures. Ember-x-int4 had ~0.55% parse_fail over 9k requests.
Liam Foster: If it's model-emitted, could be pretraining artefact or decode sampler favoring PAD/terminator tokens. If runtime is adding something during streaming flush, that's a bug too. Two investigation tracks: token-level bisect vs runtime flush audit.
Natalie Ortiz: Agreed. Mitigations: 1) gatekeeper sanitizer to optionally strip terminal control bytes (NUL, BEL, ESC) when they appear after JSON close. 2) onboarding lint that flags models emitting control bytes > threshold. 3) runtime: ensure stream flush doesn't append sentinel bytes.
Priya Shah: I propose gatekeeper config: `structured_output.terminator_policy: ["fail","strip_terminal_controls"]` default `fail`. And `telemetry.terminator_tag=true` to record sanitizer events and original raw payloads to ephemeral debug logs.
Liam Foster: Important: stripping could hide a real model regression. Make sanitizer opt-in for canaries and staging only; require explicit enable flag in onboarding YAML. Also emit a coercion metric and create an alert if coercion_rate > 0.2%.
Natalie Ortiz: For onboarding lint: block models if control_byte_rate > 0.1% across sample corpus. Add a token-bisect job to check if tokenization differences vs baseline correlate.
Priya Shah: I'll open repro with a set of failing traces and token indexes. Natalie, can you add a fuzz test that injects control bytes at chunk boundaries to see if we can amplify?
Natalie Ortiz: Yep. I'll add the harness job that varies chunk sizes 1..6, injects control bytes with p=0.005..0.02, and reports pre/post sanitizer parse success.
Liam Foster: Runtime task: I'll audit the streaming flush path for any sentinel writes and add a test to assert we never add 0x00 after a completed JSON object. If runtime is clean, it strengthens the case it's model output.
Priya Shah: Quick decision: we will enable `strip_terminal_controls` on ember-x-int4 in staging for 48h with telemetry on. If coercion_rate exceeds 0.3% or golden-diff > 0.2% we roll back.
ops-bot: [automated] canary 2990001111 recorded: 9000 requests, parse_fail_rate=0.0055, coercion_enabled=false.
Liam Foster: Thanks. Ping me when you flip the feature flag and I'll watch runtime logs for flush writes.
Natalie Ortiz: I'll wire the dashboard slice `terminator_sanitized_count` + `terminator_coercion_rate`.
Priya Shah: Action items:
- Priya: repro issue + sample token traces (today)
- Liam: runtime flush audit + test (taking)
- Natalie: fuzz harness, lint rule, dashboard (taking)
- Ops: enable staging flag for 48h when ready
Priya Shah: Appreciate the quick turnaround. If we see a clear model signal we'll hold ember-x-int4 onboarding until we fix.
Liam Foster: Sounds good.
Natalie Ortiz: Thanks all :white_check_mark:
